concept.name: Recall-to-Catalog Impact Review
concept.targetBuyer: Small e-commerce, wholesale or distribution catalog operations team
concept.buyerProblem: Recall records and internal catalog rows often describe the same product with incomplete or inconsistent identifiers, forcing staff to compare them manually and risking unsupported matches.
concept.centralClaim: A provenance-preserving matcher can compare a bounded synthetic catalog with selected openFDA enforcement records and reproduce an independently labeled match, no-match and review-needed queue using explicit field evidence.

authorizedScope: Human approved the reviewer interface, larger benchmark, visual PDF, Manifest, independent validation, source integration, public hosting and publication on 2026-09-04. Paid services, production operational use, public alerts, medical decisions and recall-lifecycle tracking remain unauthorized.
nextAction: WS-002 is published on Vercel and GitHub. Preserve this final state and begin no new iteration until separately authorized. Release: https://github.com/lmnhd/web-data-operations/releases/tag/ws-002-v1.0.0

humanApproval.basis: The user approved the bounded proof and expansion, then explicitly replied 'Approved, please publish.' This authorizes independent validation, reviewed source integration, public hosting, signed-out verification, immutable tagging and publication for WS-002. It does not authorize paid services or production operational use.

limitations: No client posting was supplied; current Upwork evidence supports product matching and data quality generally, not this exact recall-review product.
The proof uses a synthetic catalog and cannot establish production coverage, current recall status, medical correctness, business impact or real-time operation.
openFDA data must not be used for public alerts, medical decisions or recall-lifecycle claims.
